text:
alex: Heads-up — ACME (EU tenant) filed a GDPR erasure confirmation request. They want proof that PII was removed from primary stores, backups, and any KMS-encrypted artifacts. Deadline 72h.

sasha: Ack. Main things: 1) ensure the tenant's encryption key material isn't still referenced in any HSM blobs, 2) confirm DB rows and KV caches removed, 3) provide audit log export showing deletion events.

jordan: Customer-facing note: they also asked whether sub-processors (search index provider, analytics) hold any of this data and whether we notified them. I told them we'd investigate.

elliot: Repro steps I propose for evidence collection and deletion run:

1) identify tenant_id: acme-eu
2) run: 
```bash
redwood-cli tenant export-audit --tenant acme-eu --range "2020-01-01..2026-01-01" --out acme-audit.jsonl
redwood-cli data erase --tenant acme-eu --targets db,kvs,kvcache --confirm --dry-run=false
```
Expected output: deletion ops with op_ids. Save op_ids for audit.

sasha: For KMS/HSM: we do NOT delete customer-managed keys (if they supply their own KMS) — instead we remove ciphertext references and key ACL bindings. For our managed keys, we need to confirm that any derived cached keys or wrapped blobs are purged. Elliot, can you run a key-reference scan: query our secrets index for any objects referencing tenant=acme-eu?

elliot: Running that now. Quick query I use:
```sql
SELECT object_id, storage_path, last_modified FROM secrets_index WHERE tenant = 'acme-eu' AND key_ref IS NOT NULL;
```
If result set > 0 we run a blob delete job: blob-delete --objects <ids> --reason gdpr-erasure --ticket 4521

sec-bot: audit export started by elliot (op 55421). Note: export includes system events and key-change events; excludes binary payload content.

alex: Also need retention window checks — backups older than 30 days: we snapshot retention policy says 90d for EU tenants. Nina, legal: is a backup purge request required or is a certification that backups will expire per policy sufficient?

nina: Legal: For strict erasure under GDPR, customer expects "reasonable steps" to remove. If backups are immutable for 90d, we must document that and provide alternative mitigation (e.g., offline restore controls, access restrictions). We should also offer a certificate listing exact objects deleted and a timestamped audit export. If sub-processor data exists, we need confirmation from them.

jordan: I've asked ACME to sign a DPA amendment allowing us to coordinate with sub-processors directly. Waiting on their legal. In the meantime they want a timeline and proof-of-action.

elliot: Quick status: secrets_index query returned 3 objects referencing tenant=acme-eu (obj_3321, obj_4472, obj_7720). Initiated blob-delete op 772900. DB erase job executed, returned op_id 772901. Pushing audit export to secure bucket s3://redwood-compliance/acme-eu/exports/772900.jsonl

sasha: I'll pull HSM logs for those object_ids and map any wrapped key events. We should include key rotation history and show that ciphertexts were unlinked.

sec-bot: compliance export completed (op 772900). Files: acme-audit-772900.jsonl, deletion-ops-772901.jsonl. Location: s3://redwood-compliance/acme-eu/exports/772900/

alex: Great. Nina — draft an email we can send to ACME with: 1) confirmation of deleted objects + op ids, 2) audit export link (read-only), 3) explanation of backup retention and mitigation, 4) sub-processor outreach plan.

nina: Will draft. Suggest wording: confirm steps taken, attach signed ops list, include timeline, and offer contractual amendment for sub-processor coordination. Keep technical appendix separate (logs + op ids).

jordan: Customer update queued. ETA to send: 36h pending legal review and confirmation from sub-processors.

alex: Thanks all. Tagging follow-ups: @sasha — HSM mapping; @elliot — archive delete receipts; @nina — legal note; @jordan — send when ready. :thumbsup:

sasha: On it.

elliot: done for my bits, uploading receipts now.

sec-bot: receipts-uploaded by elliot (op 772901).
